entries.title: Gaussian observation variance retention
entries.statement: Let X have a full-dimensional probability law mu on R^n, let G be an independent N(0,I_n) vector, and let t>0. For Y=sqrt(t)X+G define R_mu(t)=inf E[Var(f(X)|Y)]/Var_mu(f), where the infimum is over all f in L^2(mu) with positive variance. The conditioning is on the Gaussian observation; no independence between coordinates of X is assumed.

entries.title: Poincare implies Gaussian observation variance retention
entries.statement: DRAFT REDUCTION; independent review pending. If a probability law mu satisfies its Sobolev Poincare inequality with finite constant C, then R_mu(t)>=1/(1+Ct) for every t>0, with R defined using Y=sqrt(t)X+G and all L^2 functions. The constant C is an assumption in this direction. The proof in w350 ATTEMPT.md uses Gaussian Bessel inequality, prior Poincare, total variance and the adjoint of conditional expectation.
assumptions: Finite prior Sobolev Poincare constant C

entries.title: Gaussian observation variance retention implies Poincare
entries.statement: DRAFT REDUCTION; independent review pending. For a full-dimensional log-concave law mu, suppose deterministic t0>0 and eta>0 satisfy R_mu(t0)>=eta, with the infimum over all nonconstant L^2 functions. Then C_P(mu)<=1/(eta*t0). The posterior potential is V(x)+t0|x|^2/2-sqrt(t0)y.x, so its generalized strong-log-concavity Poincare bound is 1/t0. Average the posterior variance bound by the tower property, then combine with the assumed retention. The retention hypothesis is not proved in this packet.
assumptions: Full-dimensional log-concave law on convex support

entries.title: Uniform variance retention input for log-concave Poincare
entries.statement: UNPROVED INPUT IN THIS PACKET. Universal deterministic constants t0>0 and eta>0 are sought such that R_mu(t0)>=eta for every isotropic log-concave probability law in every dimension, where R takes an infimum over all L^2 test functions. Together with the recorded reductions this is equivalent, up to explicit constants, to a uniform Poincare bound. Linear or quadratic tests alone do not discharge this all-function hypothesis. Recent primary preprints claim the parent target; this packet has not audited their complete proofs.
assumptions: All dimensions and all L^2 functions

entries.title: Exact Gaussian variance retention benchmark
entries.statement: GAUSSIAN SPECIAL CASE; independent review of the new bridge pending. For mu=N(0,I_n) and independent G=N(0,I_n), the channel Y=sqrt(t)X+G has R_mu(t)=1/(1+t). Sharp Gaussian C_P=1 gives the lower bound through the forward bridge; a unit linear function and posterior covariance I_n/(1+t) give equality. This checks channel normalization. The reverse bridge yields only C_P<=(1+t)/t, while the prior Hermite proof gives exact C_P=1.

entries.statement: SOURCE AUDIT, 2026-10-10. The September P0017 ranking records attempted_unsolved and its old attempt proves only the Gaussian special case. The existence of these claims is checked; their full proofs are not independently certified here. Current openness is UNKNOWN in this packet, with reported resolution YES. Randomstrasse psi is the Cheeger constant; Klartag 2303.14938 psi is its reciprocal.
